meta.caveat: Thresholds/prices are time-sensitive; verify against live provider docs.

bedrock.note: Fable/Mythos on Bedrock: assuming 1,024 conservatively (512 direct — Anthropic docs dropped the explicit Bedrock override as of 2026-08 and defer to AWS's Bedrock docs; AWS side unverified)
Amazon Nova: automatic caching, threshold unpublished

gemini.note: Gemini 2.0: 75% discount tier; implicit threshold unpublished

openai.note: uniform for all OpenAI models (+128-token steps)

openai.enablement_detail: Caching is on by default for prompts >= 1,024 tokens — no request changes needed. Reuse the exact prefix; cached amounts grow in 128-token steps.
openai.ttl_summary: 5-10 min sliding; up to 24h extended retention (non-ZDR default since May 2026)
openai.read_discount: per-model 50% -> 98.75% (90% on GPT-5.x) — NOT a flat 50%
openai.write_cost: free through GPT-5.5; ~1.25x input on GPT-5.6+ (single-use large prompts pay the premium for nothing)
openai.routing: prompt_cache_key — same string per prefix-group; keep <= ~15 RPM per key
openai.batch_note: batch x caching stacking is UNDOCUMENTED (open question in the research)
gotchas: A cache entry becomes readable only after the writing request completes — N simultaneous cold requests all pay full price. Warm one, then fan out.
Discount is per-model; verify against the live pricing page before quoting numbers.
Org-level cache scope.

anthropic.enablement_detail: OPT-IN: nothing caches unless you mark a breakpoint with "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"} (<= 4 breakpoints; 20-block lookback). Render order is tools -> system -> messages; a byte change invalidates everything after it.
anthropic.action: Add "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"} on the LAST static block (end of system prompt or last stable message). For >5-min gaps use {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"} (2x write premium).
anthropic.default_min_note: unknown Claude model — assuming the most conservative tier (4,096)
anthropic.ttl_summary: 5 min (refreshed FREE on every hit) / 1h opt-in via ttl:'1h'
anthropic.write_cost: write premium: 1.25x (5-min TTL) / 2x (1-hour TTL); no storage fee
anthropic.batch_note: STACKS with the Batch API 50%: cache read in a batch = 0.1x * 0.5x = ~95% off
gotchas: Below the model's minimum the marked prefix SILENTLY won't cache (cache_creation_input_tokens: 0, no error).
Model switch = cold cache (model-scoped). Toggling extended thinking invalidates system+messages (tools survive).
Serialize tool JSON deterministically (sorted keys, frozen order) — non-deterministic serialization is a classic silent invalidator.
Concurrency: entry readable only after the first response begins streaming — warm one, then fan out.
Pre-warm with a max_tokens: 0 request to skip cold-write latency on the first real request.
On Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5: append {"role": "system", ...} to messages for mid-conversation instructions instead of editing the top-level system prompt — preserves the cached prefix.
No prompt_cache_key equivalent — routing affinity cannot be steered; identical prefixes are the only lever.

gemini.enablement_detail: Implicit caching is automatic on 2.5+ (put common content at the prompt start, send similar-prefix requests close in time). Explicit CachedContent API for guaranteed reuse (you pay storage per token-hour).
gemini.action: Implicit: nothing required — just structure static-first. Explicit: create a CachedContent object and reference its name (only worth it with real reuse: storage $4.50/M-tok-hr Pro, $1.00 Flash).
gemini.default_min_note: unknown Gemini model — assuming the conservative 4,096 (3.x tier)
gemini.ttl_summary: implicit: lifetime not user-set (unpublished); explicit: ttl/expireTime (default unpublished on the Developer API; 60 min on Vertex)
gemini.write_cost: NO write premium. Implicit = no storage either (the only pure-upside caching in the study). Explicit adds storage per 1M-tok-hr.
gemini.batch_note: 50% batch discount exists; stacking with caching is UNDOCUMENTED
gotchas: Per project / API key cache scope.
Thinking-token caching is undocumented.
Implicit cache lifetime is unpublished — don't rely on long gaps.

xai.enablement_detail: Automatic, but the cache is PER-SERVER — routing matters more than anything else. Set the x-grok-conv-id header (or prompt_cache_key on the Responses API) so consecutive requests land on the same server.
xai.action: Always set x-grok-conv-id (same value per conversation). Append-only: never edit earlier messages.
xai.default_min_note: NO published activation threshold (least-documented big provider)
xai.ttl_summary: NO guaranteed TTL — entries may be evicted at any time (biggest reliability caveat in the study)
xai.routing: x-grok-conv-id header (per-server routing) / prompt_cache_key on Responses API
xai.batch_note: 20% batch discount exists; stacking with caching is UNDOCUMENTED
gotchas: Don't rely on gaps between requests — no TTL guarantee at all.
Editing an earlier message breaks the append-only prefix.

openrouter.enablement_detail: Caching inherits from the upstream provider: automatic for OpenAI/Grok/DeepSeek/Groq/Gemini-2.5, cache_control for Anthropic/Gemini-explicit/Qwen. OpenRouter also has its own opt-in response cache (~80-300ms).
openrouter.action: Match the upstream's rule (for Claude models: forward "cache_control" breakpoints — OpenRouter passes them through). PIN the provider routing — switching upstream = cold cache. Use BYOK for privacy.
openrouter.default_min_note: inherited from upstream (and from which HOST serves the request)
openrouter.write_cost: passes through the upstream write premium
openrouter.routing: provider pinning (order/allow lists) — switching providers = cold cache
gotchas: SECURITY: the 2026 CacheProbe audit found cross-account prompt-cache leakage in OpenRouter's default shared-credential mode (Groq 100%, Fireworks p=4e-15). Mitigation: BYOK. Whether this was fixed post-mid-2026 is an open question.
The effective threshold depends on which upstream HOST serves the request (e.g. Claude direct vs Claude-on-Bedrock have different floors) — pin the provider.
Watch the cache_discount response field to verify savings.

bedrock.enablement_detail: Explicit cachePoint blocks (Converse API) for Claude and GPT-5.6; automatic for Nova and GPT-5.5-and-older. Order tools -> system -> messages.
bedrock.action: Insert {"cachePoint": {"type": "default"}} after the static content (system prompt / tool config) in the Converse API request.
bedrock.default_min_note: unknown Bedrock model — assuming the conservative 4,096
bedrock.ttl_summary: 5 min (reset on hit) / 1h on Opus-Sonnet-Haiku 4.5 / 30 min GPT-5.6
bedrock.write_cost: may carry a premium (GPT-5.6: 1.25x; GPT-5.5-: free; Claude: mirrors Anthropic)
bedrock.batch_note: does NOT stack with batch — caching is on-demand-throughput only (one of only two definitive batch answers in the study)
gotchas: Cross-platform drift: the same Claude model can need a HIGHER minimum on Bedrock than on the direct Anthropic API.
Cache hits don't count against rate limits (nice perk).
Per AWS account/region scope (cache-specific isolation undocumented).

vertex.enablement_detail: Hosts TWO vendors with different cost models: Gemini (implicit auto + explicit CachedContent, 60-min default TTL) and Claude (cache_control breakpoints, 5m->1h).
vertex.action: Gemini: implicit is on by default; explicit CachedContent for guaranteed reuse. Claude-on-Vertex: add "cache_control" breakpoints exactly as on the direct API.
vertex.default_min_note: unknown Vertex model — assuming the conservative 4,096
vertex.ttl_summary: Gemini explicit: 60 min default; Claude: 5 min (free refresh) -> 1h opt-in
vertex.write_cost: Gemini: std input + storage on explicit (no premium); Claude: +25% / +100% write
gotchas: Per GCP project/region isolation; NO cross-project sharing.
Claude-on-Vertex has a per-project opt-out.
